'''''Agapanthus praecox''''' ('''common agapanthus''',<ref name=plantzafrica/> '''blue lily''',<ref name=plantzafrica/> '''African lily''',<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=2008-07-20}}</ref>  or '''lily of the Nile'''<ref name=weedsbluemountains/>) is a popular garden plant around the world, especially in [[Mediterranean climate]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.sfbotanicalgarden.org/garden/bloom_10_08.shtml |title=In Bloom - Agapanthus |access-date=2016-12-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118230443/http://sfbotanicalgarden.org/garden/bloom_10_08.shtml |archive-date=2017-01-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It is native to the [[Kwa-Zulu Natal]] and [[Eastern Cape]] provinces of [[South Africa]]. Local names include ''agapant'', ''bloulelie'', ''isicakathi'' and ''ubani''.<ref name=plantzafrica>{{cite web|url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantab/agapanpraecox.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040305054515/http://www.plantzafrica.com/plantab/agapanpraecox.htm|url-status=live|archive-date=2004-03-05|title=''Agapanthus praecox'' Willd.|work=PlantZAfrica.com|publisher=South African National Biodiversity Institute|accessdate=2008-07-20}}</ref> Most of the cultivated plants of the genus ''[[Agapanthus]]'' are hybrids or cultivars of this species. It is divided into three subspecies: subsp.''praecox'', subsp. ''orientalis'' and subsp. ''minimus.''<ref name=plantzafrica/>

==Description==
[[File:Agapanthus praecox-IMG 8965.JPG|thumb|left|250px|Flowering clumps]]
''Agapanthus praecox'' is a variable species with open-faced flowers. It is a [[perennial plant]] that can live for up to 75 years. Its evergreen leaves are 2 cm wide and 50 cm long. Its [[inflorescence]] is an [[umbel]]. The flowers are blue, purple or white and bloom from late spring to summer, followed by capsules filled with black seeds. Its flowering stem reaches one meter high. Its roots are very powerful and can break concrete.<ref name=plantzafrica/>

===Subspecies===
;''Agapanthus praecox'' subsp. ''praecox''
This subspecies occurs in the [[Eastern Cape]] province of [[South Africa]]. It usually grows to between 0.8 and 1 metre tall and has 10 to 11 leathery leaves. The blue flowers appear from December to February.<ref name=plantzafrica/> These have [[perianth]] segments which are greater than 50 mm in length.<ref name=plantzafrica/>

;''Agapanthus praecox'' subsp. ''orientalis''
This subspecies occurs in the Eastern Cape and southern [[KwaZulu-Natal]]. Although it is  about the same height as subsp. ''praecox'', it has up to 20 poisonous, strap-like leaves per plant which are arching and are not leathery.<ref name=plantzafrica/> These range in length from 20 to 70 cm and are 3 to 5 cm wide.<ref name=NSW>{{cite web |url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=in&name=Agapanthus~praecox |title=''Agapanthus praecox'' subsp. ''orientalis'' (F.M.Leight.) F.M.Leight. 
 |accessdate=2008-07-20 |work= PlantNET - New South Wales Flora Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens & Domain Trust, Sydney Australia| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20080815023202/http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=in&name=Agapanthus~praecox| archivedate= 15 August 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref> Flower colour ranges from blue to white.<ref name=plantzafrica/><ref name=weedsbluemountains>{{cite web|url=http://www.weedsbluemountains.org.au/agapanthus.asp| title=Agapanthus - Weeds of Blue Mountains Bushland|accessdate=2008-07-20| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20080720081529/http://weedsbluemountains.org.au/agapanthus.asp| archivedate= 20 July 2008 | url-status= dead}}</ref> Shiny black seeds are produced in three-sided capsules.<ref name=weedsbluemountains/> These have [[perianth]] segments which are less than 50 mm in length.<ref name=plantzafrica/>

;''Agapanthus praecox'' subsp. ''minimus''
Occurring in the southeastern [[Western Cape]] and Eastern Cape, this subspecies is the smallest, ranging in height from 300 to 600 mm. It has a longer flowering season, from November to March. Flower colour includes white and various shades of blue.<ref name=plantzafrica/>

==Cultivation==
The plant prefers a well-drained soil, but supports a poor soil. Exposure to full sun is preferable, but it supports partial shade. It has low tolerance to being moved. It can be multiplied by sowing (flowering under 3 to 4 years) or division. It tolerates [[drought]] once well installed, but watering is preferable in case of long dry periods. It overwinters as a stump and therefore completely disappears during the cold months. Contrary to popular belief, this species can withstand wind, frost and cold up to −15 °C provided that the strains are protected for the first two years with [[mulching]].

Young [[Shoot (botany)|shoots]] need to be protected from [[slugs]] and [[snails]]. A contribution of 2 or 3 handfuls of [[wood ash]] around the stump in the spring may keep the [[gastropod]]s away and make a good contribution of [[potash]].<ref>Jean Trudel, Gardens and scenery: summer flowers, Saint-Laurent (Quebec), Book-Loisirs Ltée,1984, 65  p. {{ISBN|2-89210-229-4}}</ref>

==Naturalisation==
The species is naturalised in [[Australia]],<ref name=weedsbluemountains/> [[New Zealand]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.envbop.govt.nz/weeds/Weed229.asp |title=Agapanthus praecox |work=Weeds Index |publisher=Environment Bay of Plenty |accessdate=2008-07-20 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080621163851/http://www.envbop.govt.nz/weeds/Weed229.asp |archivedate=2008-06-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Isles of Scilly]].<ref name="Weird Weeds of Scilly">{{cite web|url=http://www.islesofscillyholidays.co.uk/TheIslander/TI_03/TheIslander3-p27-30.pdf|title=Weird Weeds of Scilly|work=The Islander|accessdate=2008-07-20|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080705155814/http://www.islesofscillyholidays.co.uk/TheIslander/TI_03/TheIslander3-p27-30.pdf|archive-date=2008-07-05|url-status=dead}}</ref> It is reportedly naturalised in [[Madeira]], the [[Canary Islands]], [[Eritrea]], [[Ethiopia]], [[St. Helena]], [[Jersey]],  [[Norfolk Island]], [[Mexico]], [[Honduras]], [[Costa Rica]] and [[Tristan da Cunha]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=293550 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref>

''Agapanthus praecox''  subsp. ''orientalis'' is highly regarded for being tough in sun and heat, long-flowering, and is a favourite for many councils in Australia for the landscaping of roads and other public areas which do not get watered. The plant is still widely planted but in some areas it is considered a weed, and planting has been discontinued,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.reportage-enviro.com/2010/05/councils-halt-cultivation-of-agapanthus-plants/ |title= Councils Halt Cultivation of Agapanthus Plants |accessdate=2012-12-23 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120611085512/http://www.reportage-enviro.com/2010/05/councils-halt-cultivation-of-agapanthus-plants/ |archivedate=2012-06-11 }}</ref> although it is not generally regarded as highly invasive.
